Accordingly, we plan to continue reporting Conversion Rate in our Forms 10-Q and 10-K through the remainder of fiscal year 2026 as a transition period, and we do not intend to report this metric beginning with our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ending March 31, 2027.
As our products and services continue to evolve, we expect to continue evaluating our key operating metrics disclosures to ensure they remain aligned with how management assesses the business.

We use Contribution Profit and Contribution Margin as part of our overall assessment of performance, including the preparation of our annual operating budget and quarterly forecasts, to evaluate the effectiveness of our business strategies, and to communicate with our Board of Directors concerning our financial performance.

We expect that our sales and marketing expenses will generally fluctuate as a percentage of our total revenue from period to period and may increase as we hire additional sales and marketing personnel, increase our marketing activities and build greater brand awareness.
We expect that our customer operations expenses will generally fluctuate as a percentage of our total revenue from period to period, and may increase in absolute dollars as we expand our portfolio.

We expect that our engineering and product development expenses will generally fluctuate as a percentage of our total revenue from period to period, and may increase in absolute dollars as we expand our engineering and product development team to continue to improve our AI models and develop new products and product enhancements.
We expect to increase the size of our general and administrative function to support the further growth of our business.
As a result, we expect that our general, administrative and other expenses will increase in absolute dollars but may fluctuate as a percentage of our total revenue from period to period.
Stock-based compensation expense has been, and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a significant recurring expense for our business and an important part of our compensation strategy.
Our cash requirements related to operating lease agreements are $80.8 million, of which $7.8 million is expected to be paid within the next 12 months.

We will continue to utilize our capital to support R&D activities and, at times, as a funding source for loans during periods of marketplace funding constraints or to bridge the timing between origination and sales of loans.
We plan to sell loans held on our balance sheet to lending partners and institutional investors over time in the form of secondary sales or securitizations and pass through issuances.

To the extent that there are differences between our estimates and actual results, our future financial statement presentation, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows will be affected.
